title.zh: 卷一百十九 列傳第五十七: 粘葛奴申 劉天起 完顏婁室三人大婁室、中婁室、小婁室 烏古論鎬 張天綱 完顏仲德
title.en: Volume 119 Biographies 57: Zhange Nushen, Liu Tianqi, WanyanLoushisanrendaloushi, Zhong Loushi, Xiao Loushi, Wu Gu Lungao, Zhang Tiangang, Wanyan Zhongde
title.raw: 卷一百十九 列傳第五十七: 粘葛奴申 劉天起 完顏婁室三人大婁室、中婁室、小婁室 烏古論鎬 張天綱 完顏仲德 Volume 119 Biographies 57: Zhange Nushen, Liu Tianqi, WanyanLoushisanrendaloushi, Zhong Loushi, Xiao Loushi, Wu Gu Lungao, Zhang Tiangang, Wanyan Zhongde

sentences.zh: 粘葛奴申

translations.literal: Zhange Nushen
translations.idiomatic: Zhange Nushen

sentences.zh: 粘葛奴申，由任子入宮，或曰策論進士。

translations.literal: Zhange Nushen entered the palace through the office of hereditary appointment; it is also said he was a Presented Scholar in Policy Discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhange Nushen entered imperial service by hereditary privilege; some accounts say he had passed the policy-discourse examination for the doctorate.

sentences.zh: 天興初，卒開封府，以嚴幹稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, he served as Prefect of Kaifeng and was known for stern efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxing reign he was prefect of Kaifeng and won a reputation for rigorous, effective administration.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，擢為陳州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, he was promoted to Defender-in-Chief of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the fifth month, he was promoted to defender-in-chief of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時兵戈搶攘，道路不通，奴申受命，毅然策孤騎由間道以往。

translations.literal: At that time arms clashed everywhere and roads were cut; Nushen accepted his commission and resolutely rode alone by hidden routes to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was torn by fighting and travel was impossible; Nushen accepted his orders and set out alone on horseback by back roads without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 陳自兵興，軍民皆避遷他郡，奴申為之擇官吏，明號令，完顏郭，立廬舍，實倉廩，備器械。

translations.literal: Since fighting had broken out at Chen, soldiers and civilians had all fled to other prefectures; Nushen for them selected officials, clarified regulations, completed the walls and suburbs, erected dwellings, filled granaries, and prepared weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Since the outbreak of war, Chen's soldiers and civilians had all fled elsewhere; Nushen appointed officials, enforced clear regulations, restored walls and suburbs, built housing, stocked granaries, and gathered arms.

sentences.zh: 未幾，聚流亡數十萬口，米一斛直白金四兩，市肆喧哄，如汴之闤鋏，京城危困之民望而歸者不絕，遂指以為東南生路。

translations.literal: Before long he gathered several hundred thousand displaced persons; a hu of grain sold for four taels of white silver, market stalls clamored like the market lanes of Bian, and people in distress from the capital looked to him and came without cease, so that it was pointed to as a lifeline to the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he had gathered several hundred thousand refugees; grain sold at four taels of silver per hu, markets bustled like Kaifeng's busiest quarters, and desperate people from the capital streamed toward him without end, until the place was hailed as the one escape route to the southeast.

sentences.zh: 明年，哀宗走歸德，改陳州為金興軍，馳使褒諭，以奴申為節度使。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Aizong fled to Guide; Chenzhou was renamed the Jinxing Army, messengers were sent with praise and commendation, and Nushen was made Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Emperor Aizong fled to Guide, Chenzhou was redesignated the Jinxing Army; the court dispatched envoys with commendations and appointed Nushen its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄拜參知政事，行尚書省于陳。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor and exercised the Secretariat at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was named vice grand councilor and directed the Secretariat from Chen.

sentences.zh: 於是，奴申立五都尉以將其兵，建威來豬糞、虎威蒲察合達、振武李順兒、振威王義、果毅完顏某，凡招撫司至者皆使隸都尉司。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nushen established five commandants to lead his troops: Jianwei Lai Zhufen, Huwei Pucha Heda, Zhenwu Li Shun'er, Zhenwei Wang Yi, and Guoyi Wanyan Mou; all who arrived from pacification offices were made subordinate to the commandant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Nushen then created five commandant offices to command his forces—Jianwei under Lai Zhufen, Huwei under Pucha Heda, Zhenwu under Li Shun'er, Zhenwei under Wang Yi, and Guoyi under a certain Wanyan—and placed every officer sent from the pacification bureau under them.

sentences.zh: 是時，交戰無虛日，州所屯軍十萬有餘。

translations.literal: At that time fighting occurred without a single idle day, and troops stationed in the prefecture numbered more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting raged daily; the garrison at Chen numbered well over a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 奴申與官屬謀曰：「大兵日至，而吾州糧有盡，奈何？」

translations.literal: Nushen discussed with his staff, saying, "The Great Army arrives daily, yet our prefecture's grain has limits—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Nushen consulted his staff: "The enemy army comes closer every day, yet our grain cannot last—what are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 乃減軍所給，月一斛五鬥者作一斛，又作八斗，又作六斗。

translations.literal: He then reduced the army's ration: those who had received one hu and five dou per month were given one hu, then eight dou, then six dou.
translations.idiomatic: He cut troop rations step by step: allowances of one hu and five dou per month were reduced to one hu, then eight dou, then six.

sentences.zh: 將領則不給。

translations.literal: Officers received nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Officers were given no grain at all.

sentences.zh: 人心稍怨。

translations.literal: Hearts among the men gradually turned resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Discontent spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 故李順兒、崔都尉因而有異志，劉提控及完顏不如哥提控者預焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Li Shun'er and Commandant Cui harbored divergent intentions, and Control Officer Liu and Control Officer Wanyan Buruge took part.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun'er and Commandant Cui therefore began plotting treason, joined by Control Officer Liu and Control Officer Wanyan Buruge.

sentences.zh: 奴申知其謀，常以兵自防。

translations.literal: Nushen knew of their plot and constantly guarded himself with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Nushen learned of the conspiracy and kept armed guards about him at all times.

sentences.zh: 及聞大元兵往硃仙鎮市易，奴申遣五都尉軍各二百人，以李順兒、副都尉崔某將之，襲項城寨。

translations.literal: When he heard that Great Yuan troops were going to Zhuxian Town to trade in the market, Nushen sent two hundred men from each of the five commandant forces, with Li Shun'er and Vice Commandant Cui leading them, to raid the Xiangcheng stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yuan forces were trading at Zhuxian Town, Nushen dispatched two hundred men from each commandant unit under Li Shun'er and Vice Commandant Cui to strike the Xiangcheng camp.

sentences.zh: 令孫鎮撫者召順兒議兵事，孫至其家，順兒已擐甲，孫欲觀其刀，順兒拔示之，孫色動，即出門奔去。

translations.literal: He ordered Pacification Commissioner Sun to summon Shun'er to discuss military affairs; Sun reached his house and Shun'er was already armored; Sun wished to inspect his blade, Shun'er drew and showed it, Sun's expression changed, and he at once went out the door and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pacification Commissioner Sun to summon Shun'er on military business; at Shun'er's house Sun found him already in armor. When Sun asked to see his sword, Shun'er drew it; Sun's face changed and he bolted out the door.

sentences.zh: 順兒追殺之，乃上馬，引兵二百人入省，說軍士曰：「行省克減軍糧，汝輩欲飽食則從我，不欲則從行省。」

translations.literal: Shun'er pursued and killed him, then mounted, led two hundred troops into the provincial office, and told the soldiers, "The provincial administration has cut your grain—if you wish to eat your fill, follow me; if not, follow the provincial administration."
translations.idiomatic: Shun'er ran him down and killed him, mounted, led two hundred men into the provincial compound, and called to the troops: "The provincial government has slashed your rations—follow me if you want full bellies, or stay with the provincial administration if you do not."

sentences.zh: 於是，省中軍士皆坐不起。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers in the office all sat and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: At that every soldier in the office sat still and refused to move.

sentences.zh: 奴申聞變走後堂，追殺之。

translations.literal: Nushen heard of the disturbance and fled to the rear hall; they pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the uproar, Nushen fled to the rear hall; his pursuers caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 提控劉某加害，解其虎符以與順兒，並殺其子侄婿及鄉人王都尉。

translations.literal: Control Officer Liu added injury, took his tiger tally and gave it to Shun'er, and also killed his sons, nephews, sons-in-law, and fellow townsman Commandant Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Control Officer Liu joined the attack, stripped Nushen's tiger tally and handed it to Shun'er, and killed his sons, nephews, sons-in-law, and a townsman, Commandant Wang.

sentences.zh: 順兒令五都尉軍皆甲，守街曲。

translations.literal: Shun'er ordered all five commandant forces to don armor and guard the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Shun'er ordered every commandant unit to arm and hold the streets.

sentences.zh: 自稱行省，署元帥，都尉。

translations.literal: He styled himself provincial administration and appointed marshals and commandants.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself head of the provincial government and handed out titles of marshal and commandant.

sentences.zh: 以劉提控語不順，斬之坐中。

translations.literal: Because Control Officer Liu's words were not compliant, he beheaded him in the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: When Control Officer Liu spoke defiantly, Shun'er had him beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂遣克石烈正之送款於汴。

translations.literal: The next day he sent Keshilie Zhengzhi to offer submission at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent Keshilie Zhengzhi to Bian to surrender.

sentences.zh: 崔立乃遣其弟倚就加順兒淮陽軍節度使，行省如故。

translations.literal: Cui Li then sent his younger brother Yijiu to add for Shun'er the title Military Commissioner of Huaiyang Army, with the provincial post as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Li sent his brother Yijiu to invest Shun'er as military commissioner of the Huaiyang Army while leaving him in charge of the provincial government.

sentences.zh: 未幾，虎威都尉蒲察合達與高元帥者盡殺順兒之徒，舉城走蔡州。

translations.literal: Before long Huwei Commandant Pucha Heda and Marshal Gao killed all of Shun'er's faction and led the whole city to flee to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huwei Commandant Pucha Heda and Marshal Gao slaughtered Shun'er's party and evacuated the entire city toward Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 大兵覺，追及孫家林，老幼數十萬少有脫者。

translations.literal: The Great Army perceived it, overtook them at Sun Family Grove, and of several hundred thousand old and young few escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy army caught wind of the move, overtook the column at Sun Family Grove, and few among the hundreds of thousands of refugees, young and old alike, survived.

sentences.zh: 初，奴申聞崔立之變，遣人探其事情，而順兒、崔都尉亦密令人結構崔立，適與奴申所遣者同往同還。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Nushen heard of Cui Li's disturbance, he sent men to investigate the affair; yet Shun'er and Commandant Cui also secretly sent men to arrange matters with Cui Li, and they happened to go and return together with those Nushen had sent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Nushen learned of Cui Li's coup at Kaifeng, he sent agents to investigate; Shun'er and Commandant Cui were secretly contacting Cui Li as well, and the two missions happened to travel out and back together.

sentences.zh: 順兒懼其謀泄，故發之益速。

translations.literal: Shun'er feared their plot would leak, and therefore launched it all the more quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Shun'er moved the faster to strike first.

sentences.zh: 奴申亦知其謀，故遣襲項城，欲因其行襲殺之，然已為所先。

translations.literal: Nushen also knew of their plot, and therefore sent the raid on Xiangcheng intending to use their departure to attack and kill them, yet they had already acted first.
translations.idiomatic: Nushen too had detected the plot and sent the Xiangcheng expedition hoping to catch them on the march and kill them—but they struck before he could.

sentences.zh: 劉天起

translations.literal: Liu Tianqi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tianqi

sentences.zh: 完顏大婁室、完顏中婁室、完顏小婁室

translations.literal: Wanyan Da Loushi, Wanyan Zhong Loushi, and Wanyan Xiao Loushi
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Da Loushi, Wanyan Zhong Loushi, and Wanyan Xiao Loushi

sentences.zh: 完顏婁室三人，皆內族也，時以其名同，故各以長幼別之。

translations.literal: The three Wanyan Loushi were all of the imperial clan; because their names were the same, they were distinguished by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: All three men of the Loushi line were members of the imperial clan; because they shared the same name, historians distinguish them as Elder, Middle, and Younger Loushi.

sentences.zh: 正大八年，慶山奴棄京兆，適鷹揚都尉大婁室運軍器至白鹿原，遇大兵與戰，兵刃既盡，以絛系掉金牌，力戰而死。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengda, Qingshan Nu abandoned Jingzhao; just then Yingyang Commandant Da Loushi was transporting armaments to Bailuyuan, encountered the Great Army and fought, and when weapons were exhausted tied his golden tally with a cord and swung it, fighting fiercely until death.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 8, when Qingshan Nu abandoned Chang'an, Elder Loushi—then Yingyang Commandant—was hauling weapons to Bailuyuan, met the enemy host, and when his arms were spent lashed his golden tally to a cord and fought on until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，大兵至襄城，元帥中婁室、小婁室以馬軍三千遇之於汝墳。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year the Great Army reached Xiangcheng; Marshals Zhong Loushi and Xiao Loushi with three thousand horse troops met them at Rufen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year the enemy reached Xiangcheng; Middle and Younger Loushi, as marshals, met them at Rufen with three thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時大兵以三四十騎入襄城，驅驛馬而出，又入東營，殺一千夫長，金人始覺之。

translations.literal: At that time the Great Army with thirty or forty riders entered Xiangcheng, drove relay horses out, then entered the eastern camp and killed a chiliarch; the Jin men only then became aware.
translations.idiomatic: Some thirty or forty enemy horsemen rode into Xiangcheng, stampeded the relay horses out of the city, then struck the eastern camp and killed a chiliarch before the Jin troops realized what was happening.

sentences.zh: 兩婁室以正旦飲將校，皆醉不能軍，遂敗，退走許州。

translations.literal: The two Loushi, because of New Year's Day drinking with officers, were all drunk and unable to command troops, were therefore defeated, and retreated fleeing to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The two Loushi had been drinking with their officers on New Year's Day; everyone was drunk and unfit for battle, they were routed, and fell back toward Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會中使召入京師。

translations.literal: It happened that an imperial messenger summoned them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial messenger then summoned them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天興二年正月，河朔軍潰，哀宗走歸德，中婁室為北面總帥，小婁室左翼元帥，收潰卒及將軍夾谷九十奔蔡州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tianxing the Hebei-Shandong armies collapsed, Emperor Aizong fled to Guide, Zhong Loushi became Northern Commander-in-Chief, Xiao Loushi Left Wing Marshal, gathered broken troops and General Jiagu Jiushi and fled to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianxing 2, when the northern armies collapsed and Emperor Aizong fled to Guide, Middle Loushi became northern commander-in-chief and Younger Loushi left-wing marshal; they gathered fugitive troops and General Jiagu Jiushi and withdrew to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡帥烏古論栲栳知其跋扈不納，遂走息州，息帥石抹九住納之。

translations.literal: The Caizhou commander Wugulun Kaolao knew their arrogance and would not admit them, so they went on to Xizhou; the Xizhou commander Shimo Jiuzhu received them.
translations.idiomatic: The commander at Caizhou, Wugulun Kaolao, found them insufferably overbearing and refused them entry, so they pressed on to Xi Prefecture, whose commander Shimo Jiuzhu took them in.

sentences.zh: 時白華以上命送虎符於九住為息州行帥府事。

translations.literal: At that time Bai Hua, by imperial order, delivered the tiger tally to Jiuzhu to conduct military affairs of Xizhou as acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Bai Hua delivered the tiger tally to Jiuzhu, investing him with acting command of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九住出近侍，好自標緻，騶從盈路。

translations.literal: Jiuzhu came from the inner service and loved to display himself; escorts filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhu was a former palace attendant who loved to cut a figure; his retinue clogged every street.

sentences.zh: 三人者妒之，各以招集勤王軍士為名，得五六百人，州以甲仗給之。

translations.literal: The three men were jealous of him; each under the name of gathering troops to rescue the throne obtained five or six hundred men, and the prefecture supplied them with armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The three Loushi brothers resented him; each raised five or six hundred men in the name of rallying loyal troops, and the prefecture armed them.

sentences.zh: 久之，漸生猜貳，九住亦招負販牙儈數百人為「虎子軍」，夜則擐甲為備。

translations.literal: After a long while suspicion and division gradually arose; Jiuzhu also recruited several hundred peddlers and brokers as the "Tiger Cub Army," and at night they donned armor on guard.
translations.idiomatic: In time mutual suspicion grew; Jiuzhu for his part recruited hundreds of peddlers and brokers into a "Tiger Cub Army" that slept in armor each night.

sentences.zh: 一日，九住使一萬戶巡城，三帥執而驅之，使大呼雲：「勿學我欲開西門反！」

translations.literal: One day Jiuzhu sent a chiliarch to patrol the walls; the three marshals seized and drove him, making him shout loudly, "Do not imitate me—I mean to open the west gate and rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: One day Jiuzhu sent a chiliarch to inspect the walls; the three marshals seized him and forced him to shout, "Do not follow my example—I mean to open the west gate and rebel!"

sentences.zh: 即斬之。

translations.literal: and at once beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Then they executed him.

sentences.zh: 乃召九住，九住欲不往，懼州人及禍，乃從三百卒以往。

translations.literal: They then summoned Jiuzhu; Jiuzhu wished not to go, but feared the people of the prefecture would suffer calamity, and therefore went with three hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned Jiuzhu; he hesitated, but fearing harm to the townspeople he went with three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 三帥令甲士守街曲，九住從者過，處處執之。

translations.literal: The three marshals ordered armored soldiers to guard the streets; as Jiuzhu's followers passed, they were seized at every point.
translations.idiomatic: The three marshals posted armored men along the streets and seized Jiuzhu's followers one by one as they passed.

sentences.zh: 九住獨入，三帥問汝何為欲反，九住曰：「我何緣反？」

translations.literal: Jiuzhu entered alone; the three marshals asked why he wished to rebel; Jiuzhu said, "For what reason would I rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhu went in alone. "Why do you want to rebel?" they demanded. "Why would I rebel?" he replied."

sentences.zh: 三帥怒，欲殺者久之。

translations.literal: The three marshals were angry and for a long while wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: They raged and for a long time debated killing him.

sentences.zh: 小婁室意稍解，頗為救護，得不殺，使人鎖之。

translations.literal: Xiao Loushi's intent eased somewhat and he greatly protected him, so that he was not killed; they had him locked up.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Loushi's anger cooled and he argued for mercy; Jiuzhu was spared but thrown into chains.

sentences.zh: 以夾谷九十為帥，兼權息州。

translations.literal: They made Jiagu Jiushi commander and concurrently acting prefect of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: They installed Jiagu Jiushi as commander with acting authority over Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蔡帥栲栳聞九住為三帥所誣，上奏辨之，三帥亦捃摭九住之過上聞。

translations.literal: The Caizhou commander Kaolao heard that Jiuzhu had been slandered by the three marshals and memorialized to clear him; the three marshals also gathered Jiuzhu's faults and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Kaolao at Caizhou, hearing that Jiuzhu had been framed, memorialized in his defense; the three marshals countered with a dossier of Jiuzhu's offenses.

sentences.zh: 朝廷主栲栳之辨，且不直三帥。

translations.literal: The court upheld Kaolao's defense and did not justify the three marshals.
translations.idiomatic: The court sided with Kaolao and found the three marshals in the wrong.

sentences.zh: 六月，赦至蔡，栲栳懼九住為三帥所誅，遣二卒馳送詔書於息，乃得免。

translations.literal: In the sixth month an amnesty reached Cai; Kaolao feared Jiuzhu would be executed by the three marshals and sent two soldiers galloping with the edict to Xi, and he was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty reached Caizhou in the sixth month, Kaolao feared the three marshals would kill Jiuzhu anyway and sent two runners racing the edict to Xi; only then was Jiuzhu released.

sentences.zh: 及上將幸蔡，密召中婁室引兵來迓，婁室遲疑久之，乃率所招卒奉迎。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to visit Cai, he secretly summoned Zhong Loushi to lead troops to welcome him; Loushi hesitated for a long while, then led the troops he had recruited to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to move to Caizhou, he secretly ordered Middle Loushi to bring troops to meet him; after long hesitation Loushi marched out with the men he had recruited.

sentences.zh: 七月，上遣近侍局使入息州括馬，即召九住。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the emperor sent an envoy of the Inner Service Bureau into Xizhou to requisition horses, and at once summoned Jiuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor sent an Inner Service Bureau envoy to Xi to seize horses and summoned Jiuzhu at the same time.

sentences.zh: 九住至，與中婁室辨於上前。

translations.literal: When Jiuzhu arrived, he disputed with Zhong Loushi before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhu arrived and argued his case against Middle Loushi before the throne.

sentences.zh: 時中婁室已授同簽樞密院事，上不欲使之終訟，乃罷九住帥職，授戶部郎中，以烏古論忽魯為息州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Zhong Loushi had already been appointed Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; the emperor did not wish them to litigate to the end, and therefore removed Jiuzhu from command, appointed him Master of Documents in the Ministry of Revenue, and made Wugulun Hulu prefect of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Middle Loushi had already been made associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; unwilling to let the feud drag on, the emperor stripped Jiuzhu of command, named him a master of documents in the Ministry of Revenue, and appointed Wugulun Hulu prefect of Xi.

sentences.zh: 時有土豪劉禿兒、馬安撫者自蔡朝還，以軍儲不給叛入宋，州之北關為所焚毀。

translations.literal: At that time local strongmen Liu Tuer and Ma Anfu, returning from an audience at Cai, because military stores were not supplied rebelled and entered Song territory; the prefecture's northern pass was burned and destroyed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Two local bosses, Liu Tuer and Ma Anfu, returning from court at Caizhou, defected to the Song when rations failed and burned the northern gate quarter of Xi.

sentences.zh: 是時城中軍無幾，日有叛去者，且覘知宋人有窺息之意，息帥懼，上奏請益兵為備。

translations.literal: At that time troops in the city were few, each day some rebelled and left, and moreover it was detected that Song men intended to covet Xi; the Xi commander was afraid and memorialized requesting added troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison was shrinking daily through desertions, spies reported Song designs on Xi, and the prefect, alarmed, asked the court for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以參知政事抹撚兀典行省事於息州，中婁室以同簽樞密院事為總帥，小婁室以副點檢為元帥，王進為彈壓帥，夾穀九十為都尉，以忠孝馬軍二百、步軍五百屬之，行省、院於息。

translations.literal: The court appointed Vice Grand Councilor Monian Wudian to conduct provincial affairs at Xizhou, Zhong Loushi as Commander-in-Chief with the associate commissionership, Xiao Loushi as Marshal with the post of Vice Inspector, Wang Jin as Suppression Marshal, Jiagu Jiushi as Commandant, with two hundred Loyal-and-Filial horse troops and five hundred foot troops subordinate to them, exercising provincial and bureau affairs at Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Vice Grand Councilor Monian Wudian to run the provincial government at Xi, made Middle Loushi commander-in-chief (while keeping his associate commissionership), Younger Loushi marshal and vice inspector, Wang Jin suppression marshal, and Jiagu Jiushi commandant, with two hundred Loyal-and-Filial cavalry and five hundred infantry; provincial and military headquarters were established at Xi.

sentences.zh: 將行，上諭之曰：「北兵所以常取全勝者，恃北方之馬力，就中國之技巧耳，我實難與之敵。

translations.literal: As they were about to depart, the emperor instructed them, saying, "The reason the northern troops often win complete victories is that they rely on northern horses' strength joined to Chinese craft—we truly find it hard to match them.
translations.idiomatic: Before they left, the emperor told them: "The northerners win because they combine steppe horses with Chinese engineering—we can hardly match them in open battle.

sentences.zh: 至於宋人，何足道哉。

translations.literal: As for the Song people, what are they worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: The Song, though—what are they to worry about?

sentences.zh: 朕得甲士三千，縱橫江、淮間有餘力矣。

translations.literal: If I obtain three thousand armored soldiers, to range across the Yangzi and Huai would leave strength to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Give me three thousand armored men and I could sweep the Yangzi and Huai with strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 卿等勉之。」

translations.literal: You all must exert yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 八月壬辰，行省遣人奏中渡店之捷。

translations.literal: On renchen day of the eighth month the provincial administration sent men to memorialize the victory at Zhongdu Store.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the eighth month the provincial government reported a victory at Zhongdu Store.

sentences.zh: 初，兀典等赴息，既至之夜，潛遣忠孝軍百余騎襲宋營於中渡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wudian and the others went to Xi, on the night they arrived they secretly sent more than a hundred Loyal-and-Filial cavalry to raid the Song camp at Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudian's party reached Xi, that very night they secretly sent a little over a hundred Loyal-and-Filial horsemen to hit the Song camp at Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 我軍皆北語，又散漫似之，宋人望之駭愕奔潰，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Our troops all spoke northern languages and also moved about loosely like them; the Song men saw them, were startled and terrified, fled in collapse, and very many were beheaded or captured.
translations.idiomatic: Our men spoke northern dialects and rode in loose formation like the enemy; the Song troops took them for Mongols, panicked, and fled; the Jin cut down or captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 複奏元帥張閏不遵約束，失亡軍士，乞正典刑。

translations.literal: They again memorialized that Marshal Zhang Run did not observe regulations, lost and wasted soldiers, and begged proper statutory punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They also reported that Marshal Zhang Run had disobeyed orders and lost troops, asking that he be punished by law.

sentences.zh: 婁室表閏無罪，上遣人赦之，比至，已死獄中。

translations.literal: Loushi memorialized that Run was without guilt; the emperor sent men to pardon him, but by the time they arrived he had already died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Loushi petitioned that Zhang Run was innocent; the emperor sent a pardon, but it arrived after Run had died in custody.

sentences.zh: 蓋閏為婁室腹心，九住之獄皆閏發之。

translations.literal: The reason was that Run was Loushi's trusted confidant, and Jiuzhu's imprisonment had all been set in motion by Run.
translations.idiomatic: Run had been Loushi's intimate; it was Run who had engineered Jiuzhu's imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 兀典廉得其事，因其失律而誅之也。

translations.literal: Wudian investigated and obtained the facts, and because of his breach of discipline executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudian uncovered the story and used Run's disciplinary lapse as grounds to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 九月，以忽魯退縮，不能撫禦，民多叛去，奪其職，以夾谷九十權息州事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Hulu shrank back and could not pacify and control, and many people rebelled and left, his office was removed and Jiagu Jiushi was given acting authority over Xi affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Hulu was removed for timidity and failure to keep order as the populace deserted; Jiagu Jiushi was left in acting charge of Xi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，宋人以軍二萬來攻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Song came to attack with twenty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Song attacked with twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，乃和糴，既而括之，每石止留一斗，並括金帛衣物，城中皆無聊矣。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted, and therefore they made equitable purchases, then requisitioned; of each shi only one dou was left, and they also requisitioned gold, silk, and clothing—the whole city was desperate.
translations.idiomatic: When grain ran out they bought at set prices, then seized supplies outright, leaving only one dou per shi to households and stripping gold, silk, and clothing until the city was utterly destitute.

sentences.zh: 前兩月，蔡州以軍護老幼萬口來就食，北兵覺之，追及於二十裏之外，至息者才十餘人。

translations.literal: Two months earlier Caizhou had sent troops escorting ten thousand mouths of old and young to come for food; the northern troops detected it, overtook them twenty li beyond, and those who reached Xi were only a little more than ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Two months earlier Caizhou had sent an escort with ten thousand refugees to seek food; northern troops caught the column twenty li out; barely a dozen reached Xi alive.

sentences.zh: 至是，蔡問不通。

translations.literal: By this time communication with Cai was cut.
translations.idiomatic: By then all contact with Caizhou was lost.

sentences.zh: 行省及諸帥日以歌酒為事，聲樂不絕。

translations.literal: The provincial administration and the various marshals daily made song and wine their business; music and festivity did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial staff and commanders spent their days in feasting and music without pause.

sentences.zh: 下及軍士強娶寡婦幼女，絕滅人理，無所不至。

translations.literal: Down to the soldiers they forcibly took widows and young girls, extinguishing human principle—nothing was beyond them.
translations.idiomatic: Even common soldiers seized widows and girls by force, committing every outrage imaginable.

sentences.zh: 三年甲午正月，蔡凶問至，諸帥殺之以滅口，然民間亦頗有知者。

translations.literal: In the first month of jiawu in the third year, ill tidings from Cai arrived; the various marshals killed the bearers to silence them, yet among the people quite a few knew.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of jiawu, year 3, news of disaster at Caizhou arrived; the commanders killed the messengers to suppress the story, but word spread among the people.

sentences.zh: 初，諸帥欲北降，而遞相猜忌，無敢先發者。

translations.literal: Earlier the various marshals wished to surrender northward, but suspected one another in turn, and none dared act first.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders had long wanted to surrender to the north but distrusted one another, and no one would move first.

sentences.zh: 數日，蔡信哄然，諸帥屏人聚議，皆言送款南中為便。

translations.literal: After several days news from Cai clamored; the marshals dismissed others and met in council, all saying that offering submission to the southern realm would be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Within days rumors from Caizhou boiled over; the commanders met in secret and agreed that submitting to the Song was the better course.

sentences.zh: 時李裕為睦親府同僉桓端國信使下經歷官，乃使送款于宋。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yu was junior associate of the Bureau of Kinship Relations and subordinate experience officer under Commissioner Huan Duan's credentialed embassy; they therefore had him offer submission to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, a junior officer in the Bureau of Kinship Relations serving under Commissioner Huan Duan's embassy, was sent to negotiate surrender with the Song.

sentences.zh: 遂發喪設祭，諡哀宗曰昭宗。

translations.literal: They then raised mourning and set out offerings, posthumously naming Emperor Aizong as Emperor Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: They held funeral rites and posthumously styled Emperor Aizong as Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 州民奉行省為領省，丞相、總帥、左平章皆娶婦。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture honored the provincial administration as leading province; the Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, and Left Grand Councilor all took wives.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople treated the provincial government as their sovereign; the chancellor, commander-in-chief, and left grand councilor each took local wives.

sentences.zh: 十三日，舉城南遷，宋人焚州樓櫓。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day they raised the city and moved south; the Song burned the prefectural towers and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth they evacuated the city southward; the Song burned its towers and palisades.

sentences.zh: 州人老幼渡淮南行，入羅山，委曲之信陽。

translations.literal: Old and young of the prefecture crossed the Huai going south, entered Luoshan, and by winding routes reached Xinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old crossed the Huai, entered the Luoshan region, and wound their way toward Xinyang.

sentences.zh: 北兵見火起，追及之，無有免者，且誅索行省已下官屬於宋。

translations.literal: Northern troops saw the fires rise, overtook them, and none escaped; moreover they demanded and searched out officials from the provincial administration downward from the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops saw the fires, overtook the column, and spared almost no one; they also demanded that the Song hand over the provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 宋人令官屬入城，托以犒賞，從萬戶以上六七百人皆殺之，軍中亦有奪命死敵者。

translations.literal: The Song had the officials enter the city under the pretext of bestowing rewards; from chiliarchs upward six or seven hundred were all killed, and in the army as well some seized their lives and died fighting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Song lured the officials into the city with promises of rewards and slaughtered six or seven hundred men of chiliarch rank and above; some soldiers fought to the death as well.

sentences.zh: 宋人諭諸軍，行省已下有罪已處置，汝等就迷魂寨安屯，遂以軍防之。

translations.literal: The Song instructed the various armies that those from the provincial administration downward had been guilty and already dealt with, and told them to settle at Lost-Soul Stockade, then guarded them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Song told the troops that the provincial leaders had been punished and ordered the rest to camp at Lost-Soul Stockade under guard.

sentences.zh: 既而與北軍接，南軍斂避，一軍悉為所殺。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they engaged the northern army; the southern army drew in and gave way, and one whole army was entirely killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: When northern forces appeared the Song troops fell back, and the entire Jin army was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 烏古論鎬

translations.literal: Wugulun Hao
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Hao

sentences.zh: 烏古論鎬，本名栲栳，東北路招討司人。

translations.literal: Wugulun Hao, original name Kaolao, was a man of the Eastern Route Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Wugulun Hao, born Kaolao, came from the Eastern Route Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 由護衛起身，累官慶陽總管。

translations.literal: Starting from the Imperial Guard, he accumulated offices to Commander-in-Chief of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Imperial Guard to become commander-in-chief of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 天興初，遷蔡、息、陳、潁等州便宜總帥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing he was transferred to Discretionary Commander-in-Chief of the prefectures Cai, Xi, Chen, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianxing he was made discretionary commander-in-chief over Cai, Xi, Chen, and Ying prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二年，哀宗在歸德，蒲察官奴、國用安欲上幸海州，未決。

translations.literal: In the second year Emperor Aizong was at Guide; Pucha Guannu and Guo Yong'an wished the emperor to visit Haizhou, but it was undecided.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, while Emperor Aizong was at Guide, Pucha Guannu and Guo Yong'an urged him to move to Haizhou, but the court had not yet decided.

sentences.zh: 會鎬餫米四百餘斛至歸德，且請幸蔡，上意遂決。

translations.literal: It happened that Hao transported more than four hundred hu of grain to Guide and also requested that the emperor visit Cai; the emperor's intention was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao delivered more than four hundred hu of grain to Guide and urged the emperor to move to Caizhou, the court's decision was made.

sentences.zh: 先遣直學士烏古論蒲鮮如蔡，告蔡人以臨幸之意。

translations.literal: He first sent Direct Academician Wugulun Puxian to Cai to tell the people of Cai of the intention to visit in person.
translations.idiomatic: He first dispatched Direct Academician Wugulun Puxian to Caizhou to announce the impending imperial visit.

sentences.zh: 六月，征蔡、息軍馬來迓，以蔡重鎮，且慮有不測，詔鎬勿遠迎。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he summoned Cai and Xi troops and horses to welcome him; because Cai was a weighty stronghold and he also feared the unforeseen, he decreed that Hao should not welcome him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month troops from Cai and Xi were called up to meet the procession; because Caizhou was a vital stronghold and the route was perilous, the emperor ordered Hao not to come out too far to receive him.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，車駕發歸德，時久雨，朝士扈從者徒行泥水中，掇青棗為糧，數日足脛盡腫，參政天綱亦然。

translations.literal: On xinmao day the imperial carriage departed from Guide; rain had long continued, and courtiers in attendance walked in mud and water, plucking green jujubes for food; within several days shins and calves were all swollen—Vice Grand Councilor Tiangang was the same.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day the imperial train left Guide. After weeks of rain the attending officials waded through mud, gathering green jujubes for food; within days their legs swelled up—including Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Tiangang.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，至亳，上黃衣皁笠，金兔鶻帶，以青黃旗二導前，黃傘擁後，從者二三百人，馬五十餘匹而已。

translations.literal: On renchen day they reached Bo; the emperor wore yellow robes and a black bamboo hat, a golden gyrfalcon belt, with two blue and yellow banners leading before and a yellow parasol crowding behind; followers were only two or three hundred persons and horses a little more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen they reached Bo. The emperor wore plain yellow robes, a black bamboo hat, and a golden belt; two blue-and-yellow banners went ahead and a yellow parasol behind. His entire escort was barely two or three hundred men and fifty-odd horses.

sentences.zh: 行次城中，僧道父老拜伏道左，上遣近侍諭以「國家涵養汝輩百有餘年，今朕無德，令爾塗炭。

translations.literal: Passing through the city, monks, Daoists, and elders bowed prostrate on the left of the road; the emperor sent a close attendant to instruct them, "The state has nourished you for more than a hundred years; now I lack virtue and have made you suffer smearing and burning.
translations.idiomatic: As he passed through the town, monks, Daoist priests, and elders kowtowed along the road. A close attendant relayed his words: "The state has sustained you for more than a century; I lack the virtue to have spared you this ruin.

sentences.zh: 朕亦無足言者，汝輩無忘祖宗之德可也。」

translations.literal: I too have nothing worth saying; you need only not forget the virtue of the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: I have little else to say—only do not forget the grace of our forebears."

sentences.zh: 皆呼萬歲，泣下。

translations.literal: All shouted "Long live the emperor!" and wept.
translations.idiomatic: All cried "Long live the emperor!" through their tears.

sentences.zh: 留一日，進亳之南六十裏，避雨雙溝寺中，蒿艾滿目，無一人跡，上太息曰：「生靈盡矣。」

translations.literal: They stayed one day, advanced sixty li south of Bo, and sheltered from rain at Shuanggou Temple; artemisia filled the eyes and not a single person's trace was seen; the emperor sighed deeply and said, "Living creatures are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After a day's halt they pressed sixty li south of Bo and took shelter from rain at Shuanggou Temple—artemisia everywhere, not a soul in sight. The emperor sighed: "The land is dead.

sentences.zh: 為之一慟。

translations.literal: At this he sobbed once.
translations.idiomatic: He wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 是日，小婁室自息來迓，得馬二百。

translations.literal: That day Xiao Loushi came from Xi to welcome him and obtained two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: That day Younger Loushi rode out from Xi to meet him with two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 己亥，入蔡。

translations.literal: On jihai day they entered Cai.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day the emperor entered Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡之父老千人羅拜於道，見上儀衛蕭條，莫不感泣，上亦歔欷者久之。

translations.literal: A thousand elders of Cai lined the road in prostration; seeing the emperor's guards sparse and bleak, none failed to be moved to tears; the emperor also sobbed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand Caizhou elders lined the road in homage; seeing the emperor's meager escort, all wept, and the emperor sobbed for a long time himself.

sentences.zh: 七月，以鎬為御史大夫，總帥如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Hao was made Censor-in-Chief, with Commander-in-Chief as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Hao was appointed censor-in-chief while retaining his command.

sentences.zh: 初，鎬守蔡，門禁甚嚴，男女樵采，必以墨識其面，人有以錢出者，十取一分有半以贍軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hao guarded Cai, gate prohibitions were very strict; men and women gathering firewood must have ink marks on their faces; those who went out with money had one part and a half in ten taken to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: While Hao had held Caizhou, security had been draconian: men and women who gathered fuel were ink-marked on the face, and anyone leaving with cash paid a fifteen-percent levy for the army.

sentences.zh: 上至蔡，或言其非便，即弛其禁。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Cai, some said this was not convenient, and the prohibitions were at once relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived, advisers said the restrictions were unwise, and Hao lifted them at once.

sentences.zh: 時大兵去遠，商販頗集，小民鼓舞，以為複見太平，公私宿釀，一日俱盡。

translations.literal: At that time the Great Army had gone far; merchants gathered in numbers; common people were elated, thinking they again saw peace; public and private overnight brewed wine, and in one day it was all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy army far away, traders returned; commoners rejoiced as if peace had come back; public and private cellars were broached and drained in a single day.

sentences.zh: 郾城土豪盧進殺其長吏，自稱招撫使，以前關、陝帥府經歷範天保為副。

translations.literal: The local strongman Lu Jin of Yancheng killed his chief official, styled himself Pacification Commissioner, and made Fan Tianbao, former experience officer of the Guan-Shaan commandery headquarters, his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At Yancheng the local boss Lu Jin murdered the magistrate, proclaimed himself pacification commissioner, and made Fan Tianbao—formerly on the Guan-Shaan command staff—his deputy.

sentences.zh: 至是，天保來見，進麥三百石及麞鹿脯、茶、蜜等物，遂賜進金牌，加天保官，自是進物者踵至。

translations.literal: By this time Tianbao came to audience, presenting three hundred shi of wheat and deer jerky, tea, honey, and other goods; they then bestowed on Jin a golden tally, added to Tianbao's office, and from this time presenters of goods arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tianbao then came to court with three hundred shi of wheat, venison, tea, honey, and other gifts; Lu Jin received a golden tally and Tianbao a promotion, and tributary offerings soon poured in.

sentences.zh: 既而遣內侍殿頭宋珪與鎬妻選室女備後宮，已得數人，右丞忽斜虎諫曰：「小民無知，將謂陛下駐蹕以來，不聞恢復遠略，而先求處女以示久居。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they sent Inner Service Bureau Chief Song Gui and Hao's wife to select palace women for the rear apartments; several had already been obtained when Right Chancellor Husalahu remonstrated, saying, "Common people are ignorant; they will think that since Your Majesty's halting residence, they have not heard of recovering distant strategy, yet first seek maidens to show long residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor sent Inner Service chief Song Gui and Hao's wife to recruit palace women; several had been chosen when Right Chancellor Husalahu objected: "The people are simple-minded—they will say that since Your Majesty halted here they have heard nothing of reconquest, only that you are gathering girls as if settling in for good.

sentences.zh: 民愚而神，不可不畏。」

translations.literal: The people are foolish yet numinous—this cannot but be feared."
translations.idiomatic: The masses may be ignorant, but they sense what rulers do—this must be feared."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕以六宮失散，左右無人，故令采擇。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Because the six palaces are scattered and lost and those at my side are none, I therefore ordered selection.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "My consorts are scattered and I have no attendants—that is why I ordered the search.

sentences.zh: 今承規誨，敢不敬從。

translations.literal: Now receiving your admonition and instruction, how dare I not respectfully follow?
translations.idiomatic: Hearing your counsel, how could I refuse to obey?

sentences.zh: 止留解文義者一人，餘皆放遣。」

translations.literal: Keep only one who understands literary meaning; the rest all release and send away."
translations.idiomatic: Keep only one woman who can read texts; send the rest away."

sentences.zh: 是時，從官近侍率皆窮乏，悉取給於鎬，鎬亦不能人滿其欲，日夕交譖於上，甚以尚食闕供為言。

translations.literal: At that time attending officials and close attendants were mostly destitute and all took supplies from Hao; Hao also could not satisfy each person's desires, and day and night they slandered him to the emperor, greatly speaking of the Imperial Commissary's lack of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and inner staff were penniless and all looked to Hao for support; he could not satisfy everyone, and they slandered him daily to the emperor, chiefly complaining that the imperial kitchens went unfed.

sentences.zh: 上怒，雖擢拜大夫，而召見特疏。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; although he promoted and appointed him Grand Master, audiences were especially sparse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry; though he had promoted Hao to grand master, he rarely summoned him.

sentences.zh: 小婁室之在息州也，與石抹九住有隙，怨鎬為九住辨曲直。

translations.literal: When Xiao Loushi was at Xizhou he had a rift with Shimo Jiuzhu and resented Hao for arguing right and wrong on Jiuzhu's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Loushi had quarreled with Shimo Jiuzhu at Xi Prefecture and resented Hao for taking Jiuzhu's side.

sentences.zh: 及上幸蔡，婁室見於雙溝，因厚誣鎬罪，上頗信之。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Cai, Loushi was received at Shuanggou and therefore heavily slandered Hao with crimes; the emperor quite believed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Caizhou, Loushi met him at Shuanggou and heaped false charges on Hao, which the emperor largely believed.

sentences.zh: 鎬自知被讒，憂憤郁抑，常稱疾在告。

translations.literal: Hao knew himself to be slandered, was worried, angry, and depressed, and often claimed illness and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had been slandered, Hao grew anxious and withdrawn and often pleaded illness to avoid court.

sentences.zh: 會前參知政事石盞女魯歡侄大安來，以女魯歡無反狀，為官奴所殺，白尚書省求改正，尚書省以聞。

translations.literal: It happened that the nephew Da'an of former Vice Grand Councilor Shizhan Nüluan came, stating that Nüluan had no signs of rebellion yet was killed by Pucha Guannu, reported to the Secretariat requesting correction, and the Secretariat informed upward.
translations.idiomatic: Former Vice Grand Councilor Shizhan Nüluan's nephew Da'an arrived to protest that Nüluan had shown no sign of rebellion when Pucha Guannu killed him; he petitioned the Secretariat, which reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕嘗謂女魯歡反邪，而無跡可尋。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I once said, does Nüluan rebel? Yet no trace can be found.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I once asked myself whether Nüluan was a rebel—and found no evidence.

sentences.zh: 謂不反邪，朕方暴露，遣人征援兵，彼留精銳自防，發其羸弱者以來。

translations.literal: Say he does not rebel? I was then in the open field sending men to summon relief troops; he kept crack troops to defend himself and sent his weak and exhausted to come.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if he were loyal, why—while I was camped in the open begging for reinforcements—did he keep his best troops and send me only the weak?

sentences.zh: 既到睢陽，彼厚自奉養，使朕醯醬有闕。

translations.literal: Once he reached Suiyang he richly supplied himself and caused me to lack vinegar and sauce.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached Suiyang he feasted himself while my table went bare.

sentences.zh: 朕為人君，不當語此細事，但四海郡縣，孰非國家所有？

translations.literal: I as a ruler of men ought not speak of such petty matters, but the commanderies and counties of the four seas—which are not the state's possessions?
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign should not dwell on such petty grievances—yet every commandery under heaven belongs to the state, does it not?

sentences.zh: 坐保一城，臣子之分，彼乃自負而有驕君上之心，非反而何？

translations.literal: To sit and guard one city is a subject's duty; he yet relied on himself and had a heart arrogant toward his ruler—if not rebellion, what?
translations.idiomatic: A subject's duty is to hold a city for his lord; Nüluan acted as if he alone mattered and looked down on his sovereign—if that is not treason, what is?

sentences.zh: 然朕方駕馭人材以濟艱難，錄功忘過此其時也，其厘正之。」

translations.literal: Yet I am now driving and controlling talent to cross hardship; recording merit and forgetting faults—this is the time; let it be corrected and set right."
translations.idiomatic: Still, I must use every able man in this crisis; now is the time to reward service and overlook faults—set his record straight."

sentences.zh: 群臣知上意之在鎬也，數為右丞仲德言之。

translations.literal: The various ministers knew the emperor's intent lay with Hao and several times spoke of it for Right Chancellor Zhongde.
translations.idiomatic: The court saw that the emperor's sympathies lay with Hao and repeatedly urged Right Chancellor Zhongde to intercede.

sentences.zh: 仲德每見上，必稱鎬功業，宜令預參機務，又薦以自代，上怒少解。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhongde saw the emperor he must praise Hao's achievements and say he should be allowed to participate in secret affairs; he also recommended himself as replacement; the emperor's anger eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhongde saw the emperor he praised Hao's service and urged that he be brought back into deliberations, even offering to step aside in his favor; the emperor's anger softened.

sentences.zh: 及參政抹撚兀典行省息州，鎬遂以御史大夫權參知政事。

translations.literal: When Vice Grand Councilor Monian Wudian conducted provincial affairs at Xizhou, Hao then as Censor-in-Chief acted as Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Monian Wudian went to run the provincial government at Xi, Hao was left as acting vice grand councilor in addition to his post as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 九月，大兵圍蔡，鎬守南面，忠孝軍元帥蔡八兒副之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Great Army besieged Cai; Hao defended the south face, with Loyal-and-Filial Army Marshal Cai Ba'er as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the enemy besieged Caizhou; Hao held the southern wall with Loyal-and-Filial Army Marshal Cai Ba'er as his second.

sentences.zh: 未幾，城破被執，以招息州不下，殺之。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell and he was seized; because Xi Prefecture would not submit at his summons, they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the city soon fell he was captured; the enemy killed him after he failed to persuade Xi Prefecture to surrender.

sentences.zh: 烏古論先生者，本貴人家奴，為全真師。

translations.literal: Master Wugulun was originally a slave of a noble household and became a Complete Perfection master.
translations.idiomatic: The man known as Master Wugulun had been a bondservant in a noble house before becoming a Complete Perfection Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 佯為狂態，裸顛露足，綴麻為衣，人亦謂之「麻帔先生」。

translations.literal: He pretended mad behavior, naked with disheveled hair and bare feet, stitching hemp for clothing; people also called him "Master Hemp Cloak."
translations.idiomatic: He feigned madness, going bareheaded and barefoot in patched hemp robes, and was nicknamed "Master Hemp Cloak."

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘗召入宮，問以秘術。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong once summoned him into the palace and questioned him on secret arts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong once summoned him to court to inquire about occult arts.

sentences.zh: 因出入大長主家，殊有穢跡，上微聞之，敕有司掩捕，已逃去。

translations.literal: Because he went in and out of the Grand Princess's household he had especially foul traces; the emperor faintly heard of it and ordered the authorities to seize him secretly, but he had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: He frequented the Grand Princess's household with scandalous results; the emperor heard rumors and ordered his arrest, but he had already fled.

sentences.zh: 正大末，從鎬來官汝南，人皆知與其妻通，而鎬不知。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengda he followed Hao to take office at Runan; everyone knew he had relations with Hao's wife, but Hao did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhengda reign he followed Hao to Runan; everyone knew he was sleeping with Hao's wife, though Hao himself did not.

sentences.zh: 生不自安，求出，鎬為營道宇，親率僧道送使居之。

translations.literal: The master was not at ease himself and requested to leave; Hao built a Daoist abbey for him and personally led monks and Daoists to send and install him there.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, the priest asked to withdraw; Hao built him a chapel and escorted him there with monks and Daoists.

sentences.zh: 車駕將至蔡，生欲遁無所往，因自言能使軍士服氣不費糧。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to reach Cai, the master wished to flee but had nowhere to go, and therefore said of himself that he could make soldiers ingest qi and not expend grain.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor approached Caizhou the priest had nowhere to run and claimed he could teach soldiers to live on breath alone without grain.

sentences.zh: 右丞仲德知其妄，乃奏：「欲如田單假神師退敵之意，授一真人之號，旋出奇計，北兵信巫必駭異之，或可以有成功。」

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Zhongde knew his falsity and therefore memorialized, "Wishing like Tian Dan to borrow a divine master to repel the enemy's intent, grant one title of True Man, then swiftly produce a strange plan—the northern troops believe in shamans and will surely be startled and amazed; perhaps success can be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde knew he was a fraud but memorialized: "As Tian Dan once used a 'divine teacher' to rout the enemy, we might grant this man the title of True Man and try some stratagem—the northerners are superstitious and may be shaken; success is possible."

sentences.zh: 參政天綱以為不可，遂止。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councilor Tiangang thought it could not be done, and it was therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Tiangang objected, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 複求入見，言有詭計可以退敵。

translations.literal: He again requested audience, saying he had a crafty plan that could repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for another audience, claiming a trick that would drive the enemy away.

sentences.zh: 及見，長揖不拜，且多大言，欲出說大帥噴盞為脫身計。

translations.literal: When he was received he made a long bow without prostration, and moreover spoke many great words, wishing to go out and persuade the great commander Penzhan as a plan to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Received at court, he bowed without kneeling and boasted wildly, proposing to go out and persuade the enemy commander as a way to save himself.

sentences.zh: 時郎中移剌克忠、員外郎王鶚具以向者「麻帔」為言，上怒殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Master of Documents Yila Kezhong and Vice Director Wang E together spoke of his former "Hemp Cloak" conduct; the emperor in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Director Yila Kezhong and Vice Director Wang E recounted his past as "Master Hemp Cloak"; the emperor had him executed in a rage.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：晉劉越石長於撫納，短於駕馭，以故取敗。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Jin's Liu Yueshi was skilled at comforting and accepting, short at driving and controlling, and therefore met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Liu Yueshi of Jin excelled at winning men over but failed at controlling them, and so he was ruined.

sentences.zh: 粘葛奴申陳州之事，殆類之矣。

translations.literal: Zhange Nushen's affairs at Chenzhou nearly resemble this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhange Nushen's story at Chenzhou is much the same.

sentences.zh: 三婁室皆金內族，唯大婁室死得其所，其兩婁室讒賊人也，襄城事急，醉不能軍，乃逭一死，金失政刑，一至於是。

translations.literal: The three Loushi were all of the Jin imperial clan; only Da Loushi died in his proper place; the other two Loushi were slanderers and villains—when Xiangcheng affairs were urgent they were drunk and could not command troops, yet escaped death; Jin lost proper government and punishment, reaching to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: All three Loushi were imperial clansmen; only Elder Loushi died as a soldier should. The other two were traitorous slanderers who, when Xiangcheng was in peril, were too drunk to fight yet escaped punishment—proof of how far Jin government and justice had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 烏古論鎬幸蔡之請，雖非至謀，區區效忠以讒見忌，哀宗之明，蓋可知矣。

translations.literal: Wugulun Hao's request that the emperor visit Cai, though not the utmost stratagem, showed petty loyalty yet he was envied through slander; Emperor Aizong's discernment can probably be known from this.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's plea to move the court to Caizhou was not brilliant strategy, yet his loyal service earned him slander and suspicion—by which one may gauge Emperor Aizong's judgment.

sentences.zh: 張天綱

translations.literal: Zhang Tiangang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiangang

sentences.zh: 扶溝縣招撫司知事劉昌祖上封事，請大舉伐宋，其略雲：「官軍在前，饑民在後，南踐江、惟，西入邑、蜀。」

translations.literal: Liu Changzu, Commissioner of the Fugou County Pacification Office, submitted a sealed memorial requesting a great campaign against Song; the summary said, "Government troops in front, starving people behind, south treading the Yangzi and Huai, west entering Yi and Shu."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changzu, commissioner of the Fugou County pacification office, submitted a sealed memorial urging a major campaign against the Song, proposing that "regular troops advance in front with hungry civilians behind, striking south across the Yangzi and Huai and west into Yi and Shu."

sentences.zh: 頗合上意。

translations.literal: This quite matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The plan rather pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上命天綱面詰其蘊藉，召與語無可取者，然重違上命，且恐閉塞言路，奏以為尚書省委差官。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Tiangang to question him in person on his reserves of learning; summoned and conversed with him—there was nothing worth taking; yet he heavily violated the emperor's command and also feared blocking the path of speech, and memorialized to make him a Secretariat dispatched official.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhang Tiangang to examine Liu in person; after questioning him he found nothing of substance, yet he hesitated to defy the throne outright or choke off memorials, and recommended Liu for a secretariat dispatch post.

sentences.zh: 護衛女奚烈完出、近侍局直長粘合斜烈、奉禦陳謙、權近侍局直長內族泰和四人，以食不給出怨言，乞往陳州就食。

translations.literal: Four men—Imperial Guard Nüxilie Wanchu, Inner Service Bureau Direct Chief Nihehan Xielie, Attendant-in-Ordinary Chen Qian, and Acting Inner Service Bureau Direct Chief Inner Clan Taihe—because food was not supplied uttered resentful words and begged to go to Chenzhou for food.
translations.idiomatic: Four men of the guard and inner service—Nüxilie Wanchu, Nihehan Xielie, Chen Qian, and the inner-clan officer Taihe—complained that rations failed and asked leave to go to Chenzhou to eat.

sentences.zh: 天綱奏令監之出門任所往。

translations.literal: Tiangang memorialized ordering them placed under supervision out the gate, leaving them to go where they would.
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang recommended that they be escorted out the gate and allowed to go wherever they pleased.

sentences.zh: 才出及汝南岸，遇北兵皆見殺，時人快之。

translations.literal: They had barely gone out and reached the south bank of the Ru when they met northern troops and were all killed; people of the time were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: They had scarcely crossed to the south bank of the Ru when northern troops killed them all, to general satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 妖人烏古論先生者自言能使軍士服氣，可不費糧。

translations.literal: The sorcerer Master Wugulun said of himself that he could make soldiers ingest qi and need not expend grain.
translations.idiomatic: The charlatan Master Wugulun claimed he could teach soldiers to live without grain by breathing exercises.

sentences.zh: 右丞仲德援田單故事，欲假其術以駭敵，語在《烏古論鎬傳》。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Zhongde cited Tian Dan's precedent, wishing to borrow his technique to startle the enemy—the words are in the "Biography of Wugulun Hao."
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Zhongde cited Tian Dan's precedent and wished to use the trick to frighten the enemy, as related in the biography of Wugulun Hao.

sentences.zh: 上頗然之，天綱力辨以為不可，遂止，且曰：「向非張天綱，幾為此賊所誑。」

translations.literal: The emperor was quite persuaded; Tiangang forcefully argued that it could not be done, and it was stopped; he also said, "Had it not been for Zhang Tiangang, we would nearly have been deceived by this villain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was inclined to agree, but Zhang Tiangang argued fiercely against it and the scheme was dropped; he added, "But for Zhang Tiangang we would almost have been duped by that rogue."

sentences.zh: 軍吏石抹虎兒者求見仲德，自謂有奇計退敵，出馬面具如獅子狀而惡，別制青麻布為足、尾，因言：「北兵所恃者馬而已，欲制其人，先制其馬。

translations.literal: Army clerk Shimo Hu'er requested to see Zhongde, saying of himself that he had a strange plan to repel the enemy; he produced a horse mask like a lion, fierce in appearance, and separately made blue hemp cloth for legs and tail, and therefore said, "The northern troops rely on horses alone; wishing to control their men, first control their horses.
translations.idiomatic: An army clerk named Shimo Hu'er asked to see Zhongde with a "wonder plan": he showed a fierce lion-mask for horses and blue hemp legs and tail, saying, "The northerners depend on their horses—beat the horses and you beat the men.

sentences.zh: 如我軍進戰，尋少卻，彼必來追。

translations.literal: If our army advances to battle and shortly after withdraws a little, they will surely come in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: If our army attacks and then feigns a brief retreat, they will pursue.

sentences.zh: 我以馴騎百餘皆此狀，仍系大鈴于頸，壯士乘之，以突彼騎，騎必驚逸，我軍鼓噪繼其後，此田單所以破燕也。」

translations.literal: We use more than a hundred trained horses all in this guise, still tying large bells on the neck; stalwart men ride them to burst upon their cavalry—the cavalry will surely be startled and bolt; our army drums and shouts following after—this is how Tian Dan broke Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Send a hundred docile horses fitted with these masks and great bells on the neck, with strong riders to charge the enemy cavalry—they will panic and bolt, and our men can drum and yell in pursuit. That is how Tian Dan defeated Yan."

sentences.zh: 天綱曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Tiangang said, "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiangang said, "No.

sentences.zh: 彼眾我寡，此不足恃，縱使驚去，安保其不復來乎？

translations.literal: They are many and we few; this is not sufficient to rely on; even if they are startled away, how can we secure that they will not come again?
translations.idiomatic: They outnumber us; this trick is unreliable—even if it scares them off once, what keeps them from returning?

sentences.zh: 恐徒費工物，只取敵人笑耳。」

translations.literal: I fear we would vainly waste labor and materials, only inviting the enemy's laughter."
translations.idiomatic: We would waste effort and material for nothing but the enemy's mockery."

sentences.zh: 乃罷之。

translations.literal: and therefore abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 蔡城破，為宋將孟珙得之，檻車械至臨安，備禮告廟。

translations.literal: When Cai city fell he was obtained by Song general Meng Gong, placed in a caged cart and shackled to Lin'an, and with full rites reported to the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Caizhou fell, Song general Meng Gong took him, sent him in a cage to Lin'an, and presented him at the ancestral temple with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 既而，命臨安知府薛瓊問曰：「有何面目到此？」

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, ordering Lin'an Prefect Xue Qiong to question him, he said, "With what face do you come here?"
translations.idiomatic: The Lin'an prefect Xue Qiong was ordered to interrogate him: "What face do you have to show here?"

sentences.zh: 天綱對曰：「國之興亡，何代無之。

translations.literal: Tiangang replied, "The rise and fall of states—what generation lacks them?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiangang answered, "Dynasties rise and fall in every age.

sentences.zh: 我金之亡，比汝二帝何如？」

translations.literal: Our Jin's fall—compared with your two emperors, how is it?"
translations.idiomatic: How does the fall of our Jin compare with what became of your two emperors?"

sentences.zh: 瓊大叱曰：「曳去。」

translations.literal: Qiong greatly shouted, "Drag him away."
translations.idiomatic: Qiong roared, "Take him away!"

sentences.zh: 明日，遂奏其語，宋主召問曰：「天綱真不畏死耶？」

translations.literal: The next day he memorialized his words; the Song ruler summoned and asked, "Is Tiangang truly unafraid of death?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xue reported his words; the Song emperor summoned Zhang and asked, "Is Zhang Tiangang truly unafraid of death?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「大丈夫患死之不中節爾，何畏之有。」

translations.literal: He replied, "A great man worries that death is not in proper measure—what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "A true man fears only dying at the wrong time—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 因祈死不已。

translations.literal: and therefore begged for death without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He begged for death repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 宋主不聽。

translations.literal: The Song ruler would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 初，有司令供狀必欲書虜主，天綱曰：「殺即殺，焉用狀為！」

translations.literal: Earlier, an official ordered that the confession must write "barbarian ruler"; Tiangang said, "Kill then kill—what use is a confession!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an official had demanded that his written confession call the Jin ruler a "barbarian lord." Zhang said, "Kill me if you will—what need of a confession?"

sentences.zh: 有司不能屈，聽其所供，天綱但書故主而已。

translations.literal: The authorities could not bend him, listened to what he supplied, and Tiangang only wrote "former ruler."
translations.idiomatic: They could not break him; he wrote only "the former emperor."

sentences.zh: 聞者憐之。

translations.literal: Those who heard pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers pitied him.

sentences.zh: 後不知所終。

translations.literal: Later his end is not known.
translations.idiomatic: His ultimate fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 完顏仲德

translations.literal: Wanyan Zhongde
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Zhongde

sentences.zh: 正大五年，詔關陝以南行元帥府事，以備小關及扇車回。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengda an edict ordered him to conduct Marshal's Bureau affairs south of Guan-Shaan to guard against Xiaoguan and Shanchehui.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 5 he was ordered to run the marshal's headquarters south of the Guan-Shaan passes to guard Xiaoguan and Shanchehui.

sentences.zh: 時北兵叩關，仲德適與前帥奧屯阿裏不酌酒更代，而兵猝至，遂驅而東。

translations.literal: At that time northern troops knocked at the passes; Zhongde happened to be drinking wine in change of command with the former commander Aotun Alibu, when troops suddenly arrived, and therefore drove eastward.
translations.idiomatic: When northern forces struck the passes, Zhongde was exchanging command over wine with his predecessor Aotun Alibu; the enemy appeared suddenly and they were driven eastward.

sentences.zh: 阿裏不素無守禦之策，為有司所劾，罪當死。

translations.literal: Alibu had always lacked strategies for defense and was impeached by the authorities; the crime merited death.
translations.idiomatic: Alibu had never had a coherent defense plan and was impeached on a capital charge.

sentences.zh: 仲德上書引咎，以謂「北兵越關之際，符印已交，安得歸罪前帥，臣請受戮。」

translations.literal: Zhongde submitted a letter taking blame, saying, "When northern troops crossed the passes, tallies and seals had already been handed over—how can blame be placed on the former commander? Your subject requests to accept execution."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde submitted a confession, saying, "When the enemy crossed the passes the seals had already changed hands—blame cannot fall on my predecessor alone. Punish me instead."

sentences.zh: 上義之，止杖阿裏不而貰其死。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded it righteous, stopped at beating Alibu, and pardoned his death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his loyalty, had Alibu beaten, and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 六年，移知鞏昌府，兼行總帥府事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to know Gongchang Prefecture and concurrently conduct the Acting Commander-in-Chief's Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was transferred to govern Gongchang Prefecture and act as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時陝西諸郡已殘，仲德招集散亡，得軍數萬，依山為柵，屯田積穀，人多歸焉。

translations.literal: At that time the commanderies of Shaanxi were already ravaged; Zhongde gathered scattered fugitives, obtained several tens of thousands of troops, relied on mountains to make stockades, farmed garrison fields and accumulated grain, and many people returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was in ruins; Zhongde gathered refugees, built a force of tens of thousands, fortified mountain camps, opened garrison farms, and drew people back to his rule.

sentences.zh: 一方獨得小康，號令明肅，至路不拾遺。

translations.literal: One region alone obtained modest peace; orders were clear and stern, reaching to the point that things lost on the road were not picked up.
translations.idiomatic: His territory alone knew modest peace; discipline was so strict that lost goods were left untouched on the road.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，詔授仲德鞏昌行省及虎符、銀印。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year an edict appointed Zhongde Gongchang provincial administration and tiger tally and silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 8 he was given provincial authority over Gongchang with tiger tally and silver seal.

sentences.zh: 天興元年九月，拜工部尚書、參知政事，行尚書省事於陝州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Tianxing he was appointed Minister of Works and Vice Grand Councilor, exercising Secretariat affairs at Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tianxing 1 he became minister of works and vice grand councilor, directing the Secretariat from Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時兀典新敗，陝州殘破，仲德複立山寨，安撫軍民。

translations.literal: At that time Wudian had newly been defeated, Shaanzhou was ravaged and broken; Zhongde again established mountain stockades and pacified soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Wudian had just been defeated and Shaanzhou lay in ruins; Zhongde rebuilt mountain strongholds and reassured soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 會上以蠟丸書征諸道兵入援，行省院帥府往往觀望不進，或中道遇兵而潰，惟仲德提孤軍千人，曆秦、藍、商、鄧，擷果菜為食，間關百死至汴。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor with a wax-pill letter summoned troops from all routes to enter as relief; provincial administrations, bureaus, and marshal's headquarters often watched and did not advance, or met troops mid-way and collapsed; only Zhongde led a lone army of a thousand men, passed through Qin, Lan, Shang, and Deng, plucked fruits and vegetables for food, and through a hundred deaths in narrow passes reached Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sent a wax-sealed order calling up relief armies, most provincial and military headquarters hesitated or broke up on the march; only Zhongde led a thousand men through Qin, Lan, Shang, and Deng, living on foraged fruit and vegetables, and after countless narrow escapes reached Bian.

sentences.zh: 至之日，適上東遷。

translations.literal: On the day he arrived, it happened that the emperor was moving east.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived just as the emperor was moving east.

sentences.zh: 妻子在京師五年矣，仲德不入其家，趨見上于宋門，問東幸之意。

translations.literal: His wife and children had been in the capital five years; Zhongde did not enter his house but hurried to see the emperor at Song Gate and asked the intention of the eastern visit.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been in the capital five years, yet he went straight to Song Gate without stopping home, asked the emperor's purpose in moving east.

sentences.zh: 知欲北渡，力諫雲：「北兵在河南，而上遠徇河北，萬一無功，得完歸乎？

translations.literal: Knowing he wished to cross north, he remonstrated forcefully, saying, "Northern troops are in Henan, yet Your Majesty goes far to follow Hebei—if by chance there is no success, can you return intact?
translations.idiomatic: Learning the plan was to cross north, he argued fiercely: "The enemy holds Henan while Your Majesty marches far into Hebei—if this fails, can you return safely?

sentences.zh: 國之存亡，在此一舉，願加審察。

translations.literal: The state's survival or destruction lies in this one move—I beg you to examine it closely.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the dynasty hangs on this decision—please reconsider.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗屢遣人奏，秦、鞏之間山岩深固，糧餉豐贍。

translations.literal: Your subject has repeatedly sent men to memorialize that between Qin and Gong the mountains and cliffs are deep and firm and provisions abundant.
translations.idiomatic: I have reported again and again that the Qin–Gong region offers rugged mountains and ample supplies.

sentences.zh: 不若西辛，依險固以居，命帥臣分道出戰，然後進取興元，經略巴蜀，此萬全策也。」

translations.literal: Better not go west to Xin but rely on perilous strongholds to dwell, order commanders to issue forth on separate routes to battle, then advance to take Xingyuan and manage Ba-Shu—this is the ten-thousandfold secure stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Better move west, hold the mountain passes, send commanders out on separate fronts, then advance on Xingyuan and open a campaign in Ba and Shu—that is the surest plan."

sentences.zh: 上已與白撒議定，不從，然素重仲德，且嘉其赴難，進拜尚書省右丞、兼樞密副使，軍次黃陵岡。

translations.literal: The emperor had already settled plans with Bai Sa and did not follow; yet he had always valued Zhongde and moreover praised his coming through hardship, promoting him to Right Chancellor of the Secretariat and concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with the army encamped at Huangling Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already agreed with Bai Sa and would not be swayed, but he respected Zhongde's loyalty in coming through danger, made him right chancellor of the Secretariat and vice commissioner of military affairs, and camped the army at Huangling Ridge.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，車駕至歸德，以仲德行尚書省於徐州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the imperial carriage reached Guide; Zhongde conducted the Secretariat at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 2 the emperor reached Guide and sent Zhongde to direct the Secretariat from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既至，遣人與國用安通問。

translations.literal: Once he arrived he sent men to exchange greetings with Guo Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he opened communications with Guo Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 沛縣卓翼、孫璧沖者初投用安，用安封翼為東平郡王，璧沖博平公，升沛縣為源州。

translations.literal: Zhuo Yi and Sun Bichong of Pei County had first submitted to Yong'an; Yong'an enfeoffed Yi as Prince of Dongping, Bichong as Duke of Boping, and elevated Pei County to Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo Yi and Sun Bichong of Pei had first joined Yong'an, who made Yi prince of Dongping, Bichong duke of Boping, and elevated Pei to Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 已而翼、璧沖來歸，仲德畀之舊職，令統河北諸砦，行源州帥府事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Yi and Bichong came to submit; Zhongde restored their former offices, ordered them to command the various stockades of Hebei, and conduct Yuanzhou commandery headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi and Bichong later defected to Zhongde, he restored their old titles and put them in charge of Hebei stockades as acting commanders of Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 用安累檄王德全入援，不赴。

translations.literal: Yong'an repeatedly sent dispatches summoning Wang Dequan to enter as relief; he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an repeatedly ordered Wang Dequan to bring reinforcements; Dequan refused.

sentences.zh: 仲德至徐，德全大恐，求赴歸德。

translations.literal: When Zhongde reached Xu, Dequan was greatly afraid and requested to go to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongde reached Xuzhou, Dequan panicked and asked leave to join the emperor at Guide.

sentences.zh: 仲德留之，遣人納奏帖雲：「徐州重地，德全不宜離鎮。」

translations.literal: Zhongde detained him and sent men to submit a memorial saying, "Xuzhou is a weighty place; Dequan ought not leave his post."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde kept him there and memorialized: "Xuzhou is vital—Dequan must not abandon his post."

sentences.zh: 仲德虛州廨不居，亦無兵衛自防，日以觀書為事，而德全自疑益甚。

translations.literal: Zhongde left the prefectural offices vacant and did not dwell there, also had no armed guards for self-protection, and daily made reading his business, while Dequan's self-suspicion grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde left the prefectural hall empty, kept no armed guard, and spent his days reading, which only deepened Dequan's paranoia.

sentences.zh: 二月，魚山總領張曁獻作亂，殺元帥完顏胡土降北。

translations.literal: In the second month Yushan Chief Controller Zhang Yixian made disturbance, killed Marshal Wanyan Hutu, and surrendered north.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Zhang Yixian, chief controller at Yushan, mutinied, killed Marshal Wanyan Hutu, and defected to the north.

sentences.zh: 仲德累議討之，德全不從，即領麾下十許人，親勸民兵得三百人，徑往魚山，而從宜嚴祿已誅曁獻反正，仲德撫慰軍民而還。

translations.literal: Zhongde repeatedly discussed attacking them; Dequan did not follow; he then led a little more than ten men under him, personally urged militia and obtained three hundred men, went straight to Yushan—and Acting Commander Yan Lu had already executed Yixian and returned to righteousness; Zhongde comforted soldiers and civilians and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde urged action repeatedly but Dequan refused; Zhongde took a dozen followers, rallied three hundred militia, and marched on Yushan—only to find Yan Lu had already killed Yixian and restored order; he reassured the troops and returned.

sentences.zh: 有曹總領者，盜禦馬東行，制旨諭行省討之，仲德既殺賊，德全欲功出己，殺曹黨四十八人。

translations.literal: There was a Chief Controller Cao who stole imperial horses and went east; an imperial order instructed the provincial administration to punish him; after Zhongde had killed the bandits, Dequan wished the merit to come from himself and killed forty-eight of Cao's faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Controller Cao stole imperial horses and fled east, the court ordered the provincial government to pursue him; after Zhongde killed the robbers, Dequan claimed the credit and executed forty-eight of Cao's followers.

sentences.zh: 三月，阿術魯攻蕭縣，游騎至徐，德全馬悉為所邀。

translations.literal: In the third month Ashulu attacked Xiao County; roaming cavalry reached Xu and all of Dequan's horses were intercepted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Ashulu attacked Xiao County; raiders reached Xuzhou and seized all of Dequan's horses.
