sentences.zh: 仲德時往宿州，德全以失馬故，始議救蕭縣，遣張元哥、苗秀昌率騎八百以往。

translations.literal: Zhongde was then going to Suzhou; because of the lost horses Dequan at last discussed rescuing Xiao County and sent Zhang Yuange and Miao Xiuchang leading eight hundred cavalry thither.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde was at Suzhou; only after losing his horses did Dequan agree to relieve Xiao and sent Zhang Yuange and Miao Xiuchang with eight hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 未及交戰，元哥退走，北兵掩之，皆為所擒殺之，蕭縣遂破。

translations.literal: Before they could join battle Yuange retreated and fled; northern troops enveloped them and all were seized and killed; Xiao County was thereby taken.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle was joined Yuange fled; northern troops surrounded the column and slaughtered it; Xiao County fell.

sentences.zh: 四月，仲德陽以關糧往邳州，州官出迎，就執德全並其子殺之，餘黨之外，一無所問，闔郡稱快。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Zhongde pretended to go to Pizhou on account of frontier grain; prefectural officials came out to welcome him, and he at once seized Dequan and his son and killed them; apart from the remaining faction nothing was questioned—the whole commandery rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhongde pretended to inspect grain at Pizhou; when officials came out to meet him he seized Dequan and his son and killed them, punished no one else, and the whole region applauded.

sentences.zh: 初，完顏胡土以遙授徐州節度，往帥嚴祿軍於永州北保安鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wanyan Hutu by remote appointment was Military Commissioner of Xuzhou and went to command Yan Lu's troops at Yongzhou's northern Bao'an Town.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Hutu had been remotely appointed military commissioner of Xuzhou and sent to take command of Yan Lu's force at Bao'an Town north of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時祿已為從宜，在碭山數年，又得士心。

translations.literal: At that time Lu was already acting commander and had been at Dangshan several years, again winning soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Lu had long been acting commander at Dangshan and had won the troops' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 忽土到，軍士不悅，二月辛卯夜，遂為總領張曁獻、崔振所害。

translations.literal: When Hutu arrived the soldiers were displeased; on the xinmao night of the second month he was therefore killed by Chief Controllers Zhang Yixian and Cui Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Hutu arrived the men resented him; on the xinmao night of the second month Zhang Yixian and Cui Zhen murdered him.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中張敏修，忽土下經歷官，乃以軍變脅嚴祿降北。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Director Zhang Minxiu, Hutu's subordinate experience officer, then used the military disturbance to coerce Yan Lu to surrender north.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Minxiu of the Ministry of Personnel, Hutu's subordinate, used the mutiny to force Yan Lu to defect north.

sentences.zh: 祿佯應之，陰召永州守陳立、副招撫郭升，會諸義軍赴保安鎮誅作亂者。

translations.literal: Lu pretended to agree, secretly summoned Yongzhou Defender Chen Li and Deputy Pacification Commissioner Guo Sheng, gathered the various volunteer armies to go to Bao'an Town and execute the disturbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Lu feigned agreement while secretly summoning Chen Li of Yongzhou and Deputy Pacification Commissioner Guo Sheng to rally loyal militia at Bao'an and kill the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 軍夜至，祿遣敏修召曁獻、振計事，二人不疑，介胄而至，及其黨與皆為祿所殺。

translations.literal: The army arrived at night; Lu sent Minxiu to summon Yixian and Zhen to discuss affairs; the two did not suspect, came in armor, and they and their faction were all killed by Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The force arrived by night; Yan Lu sent Minxiu to summon Yixian and Zhen on business; they came in armor unsuspecting and were killed with their followers.

sentences.zh: 徐州去保安百里，行省聞之來討，會祿已反正，乃以便宜授祿行元帥左都監，就佩忽土虎符。

translations.literal: Xuzhou was a hundred li from Bao'an; the provincial administration heard and came to punish; it happened that Lu had already returned to righteousness, and therefore by discretionary authority appointed Lu Acting Left Overseer of the Marshal's Bureau and had him wear Hutu's tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou lay a hundred li away; the provincial government marched to punish the revolt but found Yan Lu had already restored loyalty and gave him acting command with Hutu's tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 朝廷複授祿遙領歸德知府、兼行帥府事。

translations.literal: The court again appointed Lu by remote investiture as Prefect of Guide and concurrently conducting commandery headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court also named him remote prefect of Guide with acting command of the military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大元將阿術魯兵至保安，祿夜遁。

translations.literal: Before long Great Yuan general Ashulu's troops reached Bao'an and Lu fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan general Ashulu reached Bao'an and Yan Lu fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 後祿聞官奴變，一軍頓徐、宿間幾一月，遂投漣水，敏修入徐。

translations.literal: Later Lu heard of Guannu's disturbance; one army halted between Xu and Su for nearly a month, then submitted to Lianshui; Minxiu entered Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After Guannu's coup Yan Lu's army lingered between Xu and Su for a month, then withdrew to Lianshui while Minxiu entered Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔仲德赴行在。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict ordered Zhongde to proceed to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor ordered Zhongde to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 時官奴已變，官屬懼為所紿，勸勿往。

translations.literal: At that time Guannu had already rebelled; officials feared being deceived by him and urged him not to go.
translations.idiomatic: Guannu had already rebelled; staff feared a trap and urged him not to go.

sentences.zh: 仲德曰：「君父之命，豈辨真偽耶？

translations.literal: Zhongde said, "A lord and father's command—how can one distinguish true from false?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde said, "When one's sovereign commands, who weighs whether the order is genuine?

sentences.zh: 死亦當行。」

translations.literal: Even death should be met by going."
translations.idiomatic: One goes even at the risk of death."

sentences.zh: 尋使者至，果官奴之詐。

translations.literal: Shortly the messenger arrived—it was indeed Guannu's fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a messenger arrived and proved the summons a fraud by Guannu.

sentences.zh: 六月，官奴誅，詔仲德議遷蔡，仲德雅欲奉上西幸，因贊成之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Guannu was executed; an edict ordered Zhongde to discuss moving to Cai; Zhongde had always wished to escort the emperor westward in visit and therefore endorsed it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Guannu was killed; the court ordered Zhongde to plan the move to Caizhou; he had long favored a western retreat and supported the decision.

sentences.zh: 及蔡，領省院，事無巨細，率親為之，選士括馬，繕治甲兵，未嘗一日無西志。

translations.literal: When they reached Cai he led the provincial administration and bureaus; affairs great or small he personally undertook; selected scholars, gathered horses, repaired armor and weapons—never a day without western intent.
translations.idiomatic: At Caizhou he took charge of civil and military government, handled every detail himself, recruited men, gathered horses, repaired arms, and never abandoned hope of moving west.

sentences.zh: 近侍左右久困睢陽，幸即汝陽之安，皆娶妻營業，不願遷徙，日夕為上言西行不便。

translations.literal: Close attendants at left and right, long distressed at Suiyang, fortunate to reach Runan's peace, all took wives and set up businesses, unwilling to move, and day and night told the emperor that going west was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The inner staff, exhausted by years at Suiyang, were glad of Runan's comfort, took wives and set up businesses, and daily told the emperor a western move was impractical.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大兵梗路，竟不果行。

translations.literal: Before long the Great Army blocked the roads and in the end the journey was not accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enemy armies blocked the routes and the western move never happened.

sentences.zh: 仲德每深居燕坐，瞑目太息，以不得西遷為恨。

translations.literal: Zhongde daily dwelt in seclusion sitting at ease, closed his eyes and sighed deeply, taking as regret that he could not move west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde would sit alone with eyes closed, sighing over the failed western retreat.

sentences.zh: 是月，上至蔡，命有司修見山亭及同知衙，為遊息之所。

translations.literal: That month the emperor reached Cai and ordered the authorities to repair Jianshan Pavilion and the Assistant Prefect's offices as places for roaming rest.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor ordered repairs to Jianshan Pavilion and the assistant prefect's compound for recreation.

sentences.zh: 仲德諫曰：「自古人君遭難，播越於外，必痛自刻苦貶損，然後可以克復舊物。

translations.literal: Zhongde remonstrated, saying, "From antiquity when rulers met hardship and were driven abroad, they must painfully discipline themselves and humble and reduce themselves—only then can they recover former possessions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde objected: "Rulers in exile have always had to endure hardship and humble themselves before they could recover their realm.

sentences.zh: 況今諸郡殘破，保完者獨一蔡耳。

translations.literal: Moreover now the commanderies are ravaged and broken; the only one preserved intact is Cai alone.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture lies in ruins; only Caizhou still stands.

sentences.zh: 蔡之公廨固不及宮闕萬一，方之野處露宿則有加矣。

translations.literal: Cai's government offices surely do not reach one ten-thousandth of palace halls; compared with dwelling in the wild and sleeping in the open they are already an advance.
translations.idiomatic: Its government offices are far below a palace, yet they are luxury compared with sleeping in the open field.

sentences.zh: 且上初行幸，已嘗勞民葺治，今又興土木之役以求安逸，恐人心解弛，不足以濟大事。」

translations.literal: Moreover when Your Majesty first traveled in visit you already taxed the people for repairs; now again raising earth-and-wood labor to seek ease—I fear hearts will loosen and slacken, insufficient to accomplish the great affair."
translations.idiomatic: Your first arrival already burdened the people with repairs; new building projects for comfort will loosen morale and doom any hope of recovery."

sentences.zh: 上遽命止之。

translations.literal: The emperor hastily ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the work halted at once.

sentences.zh: 七月，定進馬遷賞格。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they fixed grades for presenting horses and promotion rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the court set rewards for horses presented for promotion.

sentences.zh: 每甲馬一匹或二匹以上，遷賞有差。

translations.literal: For each suit of armor and horse, one or two or more, promotion rewards differed in grade.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards varied according to whether one or more horses with armor were presented.

sentences.zh: 自是，西山帥臣范真、姬汝作等各以馬進，凡得千餘匹，以抹撚阿典領之。

translations.literal: From this time western mountain commanders Fan Zhen, Ji Ruzuo, and others each presented horses; in all more than a thousand were obtained, and Monian A was put in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Western commanders such as Fan Zhen and Ji Ruzuo sent horses until more than a thousand were collected under Monian A's care.

sentences.zh: 又遣使分詣諸道徵兵赴蔡，得精銳萬人。

translations.literal: They also sent envoys separately to the various routes to summon troops to Cai and obtained ten thousand crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent along every route to summon troops to Caizhou, raising ten thousand elite men.

sentences.zh: 又以器甲不完，命工部侍郎術甲咬住監督修繕，不逾月告成。

translations.literal: Also because weapons and armor were incomplete, they ordered Vice Minister of Works Shu Jia Yaozhu to supervise repairs; within a month it was announced complete.
translations.idiomatic: Because arms were inadequate, Vice Minister of Works Shu Jia Yaozhu was ordered to oversee repairs, finished within a month.

sentences.zh: 軍威稍振，扈從諸人苟一時之安，遂以蔡為可守矣。

translations.literal: Military prestige was slightly revived; those in the entourage grasped at momentary peace and therefore took Cai as defensible.
translations.idiomatic: Morale improved slightly; the entourage, clinging to temporary safety, decided Caizhou could be held.

sentences.zh: 魯山元帥元志領軍千餘來援。

translations.literal: Lushan Marshal Yuan Zhi led more than a thousand troops to come in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Yuan Zhi of Lushan brought more than a thousand men to reinforce Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 時諸帥往往擁兵自固，志獨冒險數百里，且戰且行，比至蔡，幾喪其半。

translations.literal: At that time various commanders often held troops to secure themselves; Zhi alone braved peril several hundred li, fighting as he marched; by the time he reached Cai he had nearly lost half.
translations.idiomatic: While other commanders hoarded their forces, Zhi alone fought his way hundreds of li and lost nearly half his men before reaching Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 上表異之，賜以大信牌，升為總帥。

translations.literal: He memorialized upward in wonder, bestowed a great trust plaque, and promoted him to Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him in a memorial, gave him a great trust plaque, and promoted him to commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 息州忠孝軍帥蔡八兒、王山兒亦來援。

translations.literal: Xizhou Loyal-and-Filial Army commanders Cai Ba'er and Wang Shan'er also came in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ba'er and Wang Shan'er of the Loyal-and-Filial Army from Xi also arrived.

sentences.zh: 壬午，忠孝軍提控李德率十余人乘馬入省大呼，以月糧不優，幾於罵詈。

translations.literal: On renwu day Loyal-and-Filial Army Control Officer Li De led more than ten men riding horses into the provincial office shouting loudly, because monthly grain was not generous, nearly to the point of cursing.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Control Officer Li De of the Loyal-and-Filial Army rode into the provincial office with a dozen men shouting that monthly rations were too small, nearly insulting the officials.

sentences.zh: 郎中移剌克忠白之仲德，仲德大怒，縛德堂下，杖之六十。

translations.literal: Director Yila Kezhong reported to Zhongde; Zhongde was greatly angry, bound De below the hall, and beat him sixty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Director Yila Kezhong reported to Zhongde, who had Li De bound in the hall and beaten sixty strokes.

sentences.zh: 上諭仲德曰：「此軍得力，方欲倚用，卿何不容忍，責罰乃爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed Zhongde, saying, "This army is effective; we are just about to rely on it—why can you not tolerate them, punishing to this degree?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zhongde: "This army is useful and we mean to rely on it—why punish them so harshly?"

sentences.zh: 仲德曰：「時方多故，錄功隱過，自陛下之德。

translations.literal: Zhongde said, "The time is full of many troubles; recording merit and concealing faults is Your Majesty's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde replied, "In these times it is Your Majesty's grace to overlook faults when recording merit.

sentences.zh: 至於將帥之職則不然，小犯則決，大犯則誅，強兵悍卒，不可使一日不在紀律。

translations.literal: As for the duty of generals and commanders it is not so—small offenses are decided, great offenses are executed; strong soldiers and fierce troops cannot be allowed a single day outside discipline.
translations.idiomatic: A commander must act differently: small offenses demand swift punishment, great ones death; fierce troops cannot be left a single day without discipline.

sentences.zh: 蓋小人之情縱則驕，驕則難制，睢陽之禍，豈獨官奴之罪，亦有司縱之太過也。

translations.literal: The reason is that petty men's feelings, if indulged, become arrogant, and if arrogant are hard to control; the calamity of Suiyang—was it Guannu's crime alone? There were also officials who indulged them too far.
translations.idiomatic: Indulge common soldiers and they grow arrogant and ungovernable—the disaster at Suiyang was not Guannu's fault alone but also officials who indulged the troops too long.

sentences.zh: 今欲更易前轍，不宜愛克厥威，賞必由中，罰則臣任其責。」

translations.literal: Now wishing to change the former rut, one ought not love and overcome one's majesty; rewards must come from the center, punishments then your subject bears the responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: We must change course: do not shrink from authority—let Your Majesty grant rewards, and leave punishments to me."

sentences.zh: 軍士聞之，至於國亡不敢有犯。

translations.literal: When soldiers heard this, even until the state's destruction they did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: The troops heard him and did not dare offend discipline even as the state fell.

sentences.zh: 九月，蔡城戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Caizhou city was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Caizhou was placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 行六部尚書蒲察世達以大兵將至，請諭民並收晚田，不及者踐毀之，毋資敵，制可。

translations.literal: Acting Six Ministries Minister Pucha Shida, because the Great Army was about to arrive, requested to instruct the people together to harvest late fields; those who could not finish were to be trampled and destroyed, not to supply the enemy—approved.
translations.idiomatic: Acting minister Pucha Shida, expecting the enemy army, ordered the people to harvest late crops and destroy any left so the foe would not use them—the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔裁冗員，汰冗軍，及定官吏軍兵月俸，自宰執以下至於皁隸，人月支六斗。

translations.literal: On bingchen day an edict cut redundant posts, eliminated redundant troops, and fixed monthly salaries for officials and soldiers; from the chief ministers down to black-clad runners, each person received six dou per month.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the court cut redundant posts and troops and fixed monthly pay at six dou for everyone from chief ministers down to clerks.

sentences.zh: 初，有司定減糧，人頗怨望。

translations.literal: Earlier the authorities had fixed reduced grain and people were quite resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When rations were first cut, there was widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，欲分軍為三，上軍月給八斗，中七斗，下六斗，人複怨不均。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and wished to divide the army into three: upper army eight dou monthly, middle seven, lower six—people again resented inequality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then proposed three grades—eight, seven, and six dou—but men complained of unfairness.

sentences.zh: 乃立射格，而上中軍輒多受賞，連中者或面賜酒，人益為勸，且陰有所增而人不知，仲德之謀也。

translations.literal: They therefore established an archery target; the upper and middle armies often received many rewards, and those who hit in succession were sometimes given wine in person; people were increasingly encouraged, and secretly there were additions while people did not know—Zhongde's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: They set up an archery contest instead; elite units won extra rewards and wine from the emperor, spirits rose, and rations were quietly increased without general notice—Zhongde's idea.

sentences.zh: 甲子，分軍防守四面。

translations.literal: On jiazi day they divided the army to defend the four faces.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the army was posted to defend all four walls.

sentences.zh: 十月壬申朔，大兵壕壘成，耀兵城下，旗幟蔽天。

translations.literal: On the renshen new moon of the tenth month the Great Army's trenches and ramparts were complete; they displayed troops below the city and banners blotted the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen new moon of the tenth month the enemy completed their siege works, paraded troops below the walls, and banners darkened the sky.

sentences.zh: 城中駭懼，及暮，焚四關，夷其牆而退。

translations.literal: Inside the city they were terrified; at dusk they burned the four passes and leveled their walls and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread inside; at dusk the Jin burned the outer gates, leveled those walls, and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛丑，大兵以攻具傅城，有司盡籍民丁防守，不足則括婦女壯健者，假男子衣冠使運木石。

translations.literal: On xinchou day of the eleventh month the Great Army with siege engines approached the walls; the authorities fully registered civilian males for defense; if insufficient they requisitioned sturdy women, dressing them in men's robes and caps to transport wood and stone.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the enemy brought siege engines; every man was conscripted, and strong women were dressed as men to haul timber and stone when men ran short.

sentences.zh: 蔡既受圍，仲德營畫禦備，未嘗一至其家，拊存軍士，無不得其歡心，將校有戰亡者，親為賻祭，哭之盡哀。

translations.literal: Once Cai was besieged Zhongde planned defenses and never once went to his house; he comforted and preserved soldiers, none failing to win their glad hearts; when officers died in battle he personally made funeral gifts and sacrifices, weeping with utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege Zhongde organized defenses, never visited home, won every soldier's loyalty, and personally mourned officers killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 己丑，西城破，城中前期築柵浚濠為備，雖克之不能入也。

translations.literal: On jichou the western city was broken; inside the city they had earlier built stockades and dredged moats as preparation; though it was taken they could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the western wall fell, but inner palisades and moats prepared earlier kept the enemy from entering.

sentences.zh: 但於城上立柵，南北相去百余步而已。

translations.literal: They only erected stockades on the wall, north and south separated by a little more than a hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: They raised palisades on the wall only a hundred-odd paces apart north and south.

sentences.zh: 仲德摘三面精銳日夕戰禦，終不能拔。

translations.literal: Zhongde picked elite troops from three faces to fight defense day and night, yet in the end could not pull them out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde led elite troops on three sides in daily combat but could not drive the enemy off.

sentences.zh: 三年正月庚子朔，大兵以正旦會飲，鼓吹相接，城中饑窘，愁歎而已。

translations.literal: On the gengzi new moon of the first month of the third year the Great Army on New Year's Day feasted together, music and drums linking one to another; inside the city hunger and distress—only sorrow and sighs.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi new moon of year 3 the besiegers feasted on New Year's Day with drums and music while inside the city starved and could only sigh.

sentences.zh: 圍城以來，戰歿者四帥、三都尉，其餘總帥以下，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Since the siege began, those killed in battle were four marshals and three commandants; the rest from commander-in-chief downward cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Since the siege began four marshals and three commandants had died, and countless officers below them.

sentences.zh: 至是，盡出禁近，至於舍人、牌印、省部掾屬，亦皆供役。

translations.literal: By this time they sent out all forbidden close attendants, reaching to Masters of Writing, tally-seals, and Secretariat and ministry clerks—all also supplied for labor.
translations.idiomatic: By then even inner attendants, masters of writing, seal officers, and ministry clerks were sent to the walls.

sentences.zh: 戊申，大兵鑿西城為五門，整軍以入，督軍鏖戰，及暮乃退，聲言來日複集。

translations.literal: On wushen the Great Army chiseled the western city into five gates, arrayed troops to enter, supervised troops in fierce battle, and at dusk then withdrew, declaring they would gather again the next day.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the enemy breached five gaps in the western wall, stormed in, fought until evening, withdrew, and announced they would return next day.

sentences.zh: 己酉，大兵果複來，仲德率精兵一千巷戰，自卯及巳，俄見子城火起，聞上自縊，謂將士曰：「吾君已崩，吾何以戰為？

translations.literal: On jiyou the Great Army indeed came again; Zhongde led a thousand elite troops in lane fighting from mao hour to si hour; suddenly he saw the inner city fire rise and heard the emperor had hanged himself; he told officers and soldiers, "Our ruler has already perished—why should I fight?
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou they returned; Zhongde led a thousand men in street fighting from dawn till mid-morning, then saw flames in the inner city and heard the emperor had hanged himself. He told his officers: "Our sovereign is dead—why should I fight on?

sentences.zh: 吾不能死於亂兵之手，吾赴汝水，從吾君矣。

translations.literal: I cannot die at the hands of disorderly troops—I go to the Ru River to follow my ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I will not die at the hands of a mob—I go to the Ru to follow my lord.

sentences.zh: 諸君其善為計。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen must plan well for yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Each of you must decide for himself."

sentences.zh: 言訖，赴水死。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he went to the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: With that he drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 將士皆曰：「相公能死，吾輩獨不能耶？」

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers all said, "The Chancellor can die—can we alone not?"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers cried: "If the chancellor can die, cannot we?"

sentences.zh: 於是參政孛術魯婁室、兀林答胡土，總帥元志，元帥王山兒、紇石烈柏壽、烏古論恆端及軍士五百余人，皆從死焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Grand Councilor Borjilu Loushi, Ulin Da Hutu, Commander-in-Chief Yuan Zhi, Marshals Wang Shan'er, Hesilie Baishou, Wugulun Hengduan, and more than five hundred soldiers all followed in death.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councilor Borjilu Loushi, Ulin Da Hutu, Commander-in-Chief Yuan Zhi, Marshals Wang Shan'er, Hesilie Baishou, Wugulun Hengduan, and more than five hundred soldiers followed him to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 仲德狀貌不逾常人，平生喜怒未嘗妄發，聞人過，常護諱之。

translations.literal: Zhongde's appearance and bearing did not exceed ordinary men; in life joy and anger never issued wrongly; hearing others' faults he often shielded and concealed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde looked no different from ordinary men, never showed anger without cause, and usually concealed others' faults when he heard of them.

sentences.zh: 雖在軍旅，手不釋卷，門生故吏每以名分教之。

translations.literal: Even in the army he never released his scroll; students and old subordinates often taught him with name and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Even in camp he kept a book in hand and lectured students and old retainers on propriety.

sentences.zh: 家素貧，敝衣糲食，終其身晏如也。

translations.literal: His family was always poor; worn clothes and coarse food—through his whole life he was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His household was always poor; he wore worn clothes and ate plain food contentedly all his life.

sentences.zh: 雅好賓客，及薦舉人材，人有寸長，極口稱道。

translations.literal: He elegantly loved guests; when recommending talent, if a man had an inch of strength he praised it to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He loved entertaining guests and, when recommending talent, praised even the smallest merit to the skies.

sentences.zh: 其掌軍務，賞罰明信，號令嚴整，故所至軍民為用，至危急死生之際，無一士有異志者。

translations.literal: When he managed military affairs rewards and punishments were clear and trusted, orders strict and orderly; therefore wherever he went soldiers and civilians served him; even at critical junctures of death and life not one soldier had a divergent intent.
translations.idiomatic: In military affairs his rewards and punishments were clear and his orders strict, so soldiers and civilians alike followed him; at the crisis of life and death not one man wavered.

sentences.zh: 南渡以後，將相文武，忠亮始終無瑕，仲德一人而已。

translations.literal: After crossing south, among civil and military generals and ministers, loyal and bright from start to finish without flaw—only Zhongde alone.
translations.idiomatic: After the southern retreat, among all civil and military leaders, only Zhongde remained loyal and spotless to the end.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金之亡，不可謂無人才也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Jin's fall cannot be said to lack talent.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The fall of Jin cannot be blamed on a lack of talent.

sentences.zh: 若完顏仲德、張天綱，豈非將相之器乎。

translations.literal: Such as Wanyan Zhongde and Zhang Tiangang—are they not material for generals and ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Wanyan Zhongde and Zhang Tiangang were surely fit for the highest civil and military office.

sentences.zh: 昔者智伯死又無後，其臣豫讓不忘國士之報，君子謂其無所為而為之，真義士也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Zhi Bo died and again had no heir, his minister Yu Rang did not forget the state's scholar's repayment; gentlemen said he acted with nothing to gain yet acted—a true man of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi Bo died without heirs, his retainer Yu Rang still sought to avenge him; gentlemen called that acting without hope of gain—a true man of honor.

sentences.zh: 金亡矣，仲德、天綱諸臣不變所守，豈愧古義士哉！

translations.literal: Jin is destroyed, yet Zhongde, Tiangang, and the various ministers did not change what they upheld—how could they be ashamed before ancient men of righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Jin is gone, yet Zhongde, Tiangang, and their fellows never abandoned their duty—how could they shame the righteous men of old!
